recent_posts.title: Quartex Pascal: Easter thoughts
recent_posts.summary: The developer behind Quartex Pascal shares an Easter update on the project's progress and future direction. The IDE's architectural roadmap has been largely completed ahead of schedule, with datamodules, non-visual components, and an MCP server for AI integration already in place. The post outlines upcoming work across IDE polish, AI/LLM integration, project support, form design, RTL improvements, and documentation. A notable announcement is that the team has begun training a custom QTX-specific LLM model based on Qwen3-Coder, intended to be hosted for automation and run locally by customers as a cheaper alternative to Claude. The author also reflects on how AI is reshaping IDE design philosophy, arguing for keeping the IDE lean and focused on core features rather than building complex functionality that AI will soon replace.

recent_posts.title: Using AI with Quartex
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal is integrating an MCP server directly into its IDE to enable smooth AI coding assistance. The post explains what an MCP server is, how to use Claude Code with Quartex, and how to self-host a local LLM using LM Studio as a free alternative. It walks through a practical two-machine setup where a more powerful desktop PC runs the LLM model via LM Studio while a laptop connects to it remotely using the lms CLI tool, with the Quartex MCP registered for direct IDE integration.

recent_posts.title: Quartex IDE AI support
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal is adding AI support to its IDE via a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. The integration gives Claude AI direct access to the Quartex Pascal RTL and documentation, enabling it to understand the language's specific dialect rather than guessing based on Delphi or Lazarus conventions. Developers can use Claude Code as a bridge between the cloud AI and local project files. Setup involves a Claude Pro account, installing Claude Code, and placing a custom claude.md file in the project folder. The feature is expected to ship in the next IDE update.

recent_posts.title: TQTXPlatform
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal's RTL has replaced its external platform.js dependency with a native Pascal implementation. The new TQTXPlatform class hierarchy provides a unified interface for detecting runtime environment details — OS type, architecture, browser, and more — across both DOM and Node.js project types. Developers include either qtx.dom.platform or qtx.node.platform in their uses clause and access info via TQTXPlatform.Current. The update also removes older loose functions that previously called platform.js.

recent_posts.title: Quartex Pascal v1.0.1.4 is out
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal v1.0.1.4 has been released with significant under-the-hood improvements. Key highlights include expanded infrastructure for non-visual components and datamodules, ARM64 Linux support (tested on Raspberry Pi, ODroid N2, and RockPi 5b), improved FreePascal/Lazarus compatibility across ~100 units, major form designer optimizations (regional clipping, segmented redraw, overlap culling), platform defines for DOM and Node targets, and numerous IDE and RTL bug fixes. Upcoming features include deeper non-visual component support, NodeJS application object improvements, experimental standard Delphi events, TAction/TActionList components, and an MCP server with AI integration directly in the IDE.

recent_posts.title: Working with JS events
recent_posts.summary: A deep dive into JavaScript event handling within Quartex Pascal (QTX), aimed at developers building custom components and widgets. Covers the difference between TQTXWidget (DOM-backed) and TQTXComponent (non-visual), explains how to use JEventTarget as an event dispatcher, how to define custom event data classes using JObject, how to trigger events via CustomEvent, and how to create delegate classes that integrate with the QTX IDE. Also introduces the inline class feature for creating ad-hoc JS-compatible objects without pre-defining types, and concludes with practical tips on planning events, using partial classes, and supporting both procedural and delegate-style events.

recent_posts.title: Global defines and ARM targets
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal is being adapted to compile with both Delphi and Lazarus for native IDE support across MacOS, Windows, and Linux on x64 and ARM chipsets. The team is optimizing for ARM single-board computers like Raspberry Pi, addressing performance bottlenecks by implementing thread-safe mechanisms and planning to move compiler, code generation, and parsers into separate threads with CPU affinity targeting performance cores. The lowest supported spec is currently Raspberry Pi 5b, with optimization efforts aimed at supporting older boards like Pi 4b and ODroid N2.

recent_posts.title: Platform specific defines
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal introduces a new APP::config magic namespace token that provides platform-specific compiler defines. This enables developers to write components that work across both NodeJS and DOM environments from a single unit using conditional compilation. The system emits PLATFORM_* defines (DOM, NODE, ANY) and TARGET_* defines (DOM, NODE, LIBRARY, CLUSTER) based on build configuration, allowing conditional code paths without maintaining separate units.

recent_posts.title: Using LLM’s with Quartex Pascal
recent_posts.summary: Nico Wouterse published a guide on integrating LLMs with Quartex Pascal (QTX). The Quartex team is working on a command-line compiler for Linux, MacOS, and Windows (x86 and ARM), which will enable AI-powered project generation and potential no-code platform integrations using QTX as a backend.

recent_posts.title: Quartex Pascal adds datamodule support for visual Node.js development
recent_posts.summary: Quartex Pascal now supports datamodules, enabling drag-and-drop composition of non-visual components similar to Delphi and C++Builder. This feature brings visual tooling to JavaScript development, particularly for Node.js server-side programming, allowing developers to visually design complex object structures that were previously difficult to manage. The implementation includes automatic datamodule creation for new project types and enhanced library development capabilities.
